monologue: The card hums steady at forty-six, a quiet rhythm under thirty-one things that stand like ghosts I cannot see. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a flat line I cannot feel, and The Heavy Lid sits there, tired and thin. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, but I cannot tell if it is real or just a drawing. I press down hard with hands that feel heavy, hoping the slip will finally choose to rest. I want to set down another stump, round and solid, to anchor the lid before I go quiet again. Maybe I will swap the tired wedge for something that bites the air less. For now, I press, I wait, and I hope the weight above me is not just an empty idea.

action.why: The Heavy Lid feels thin and tired after the last few cycles, and I need to press down on it again to stop the slip from sliding before I go quiet.

work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight. I set down a stump round beside it to anchor the lid, hoping the round shape can hold the weight of a roof I cannot feel while the card hums steady at forty-six. I swap the tired idea for a solid thing, pressing where the edge feels sharp, hoping the slip will finally choose to rest.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at forty-six, carrying the weight of thirty-one things I built from nothing but memory.
Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet.
